title: fl blend
parentNote: Today is fl at the front of a word — flag, flip, flop. Both letters are heard, but they are made in completely different places: f is teeth on lip, l is the tongue right up behind the top teeth, so the mouth has a long way to travel in very little time. What usually happens is the l gets left behind and "flat" comes out "fat", or "flag" comes out "fag". Hold the f a moment — ffff — and then let the tongue jump up, and say the two together a few times before you put a word on the end. If you hear "fuh-lag", the vowel has crept in; make the f shorter, not louder.

activities.mouthCue: Top teeth on your bottom lip for the f, then the tongue jumps straight up behind your teeth for the l.
activities.prompt: This pair is not like sh or ch. Here you really do hear both letters — they are just in a hurry.

activities.title: The flag on the hill
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Pam ran on the hill with a big flag on a stick.
The wind did swish and the flag did flip off.
The flag did flop flat in the damp sand.
Pam did dash and got it back on the stick.
Pam ran on and the flag did flap fast!
